rule: a case qualifies when its `user_query` cues >=2 DISTINCT dimensions under the product's own vocabulary, core.dimensions.cued_dimensions (which reads core.dimensions.DIMENSION_CUES). No look-alike matcher is used: the same function the fan-out itself gates on decides eligibility.
rule_rationale: The mechanism under test packs a CUED-but-UNSERVED read into a batch that is being dispatched anyway. A message that cues >=2 of the 3 dimensions is the population where at least one dimension is likely to go unrequested by the model, which is the only situation in which the fan-out can act. This is the rule the GOAL proposed and it is frozen BEFORE any run.

rules_considered_and_rejected.rejected_because: 32 of the 40 cue exactly one dimension, and in most of those the cued dimension IS the case's own expected tool (C_commute -> calculate_commute, D_crime_poi -> check_safety), so the model serves it directly and the fan-out has nothing to add.

rules_considered_and_rejected.rule: >=1 cued dimension not covered by the case's expected_tools (n=13)
rules_considered_and_rejected.rejected_because: dominated by NEGATED mentions ('no commute to worry about', 'no commute needed' -- A1/A3/A10/A11/A14/E8) and by G_memory recall turns, where the fan-out correctly declines for want of a derivable destination. Those cases contribute a guaranteed zero to BOTH arms and would dilute the coverage metric without adding information.

known_limitation: n = 8 cases. The cluster bootstrap resamples CASES, so 8 is the effective resampling unit no matter how many repeats are run; the CIs will be wide and the study is underpowered for small effects. Repeats were raised to 12 to shrink WITHIN-case noise on the paired discrete counters, not to inflate the bootstrap n. Reported as a limitation rather than fixed by widening the filter (GOAL rule 4.2).
